result:
I'm going with my pick on how to build it and starting the write-up next. You've given me the what; the how is a quick call, and here's mine so you can veto it before I put it on paper.

**Add batch tracking to the taproom app you already run on the Pi.** It would get new tables for batches, ingredient lots and bottling runs, plus a few simple pages: start a batch, scan a sack when it's opened, record a bottling run and print its labels. One app, one database, one machine to look after. A bottle's batch number leads straight to its sack lot numbers.

Why not the alternatives:
- **A separate app on the same Pi** keeps the brewing side apart from the tabs. But it means two things to run, back up and keep alive, and nothing here gets better for it.
- **Off-the-shelf brewery software or a shared spreadsheet** might be quicker to start. But it wouldn't scan the sacks the way you described, and it wouldn't talk to your label printer. That leaves wet hands typing lot numbers, which is the thing you said won't happen.

This is a project rather than a quick change, so it gets a proper design document in `specs/`. Before you see it, a reviewer will read it as if they had to build from it. I may come back once with a few questions only you can answer. If not, I'll hand you the finished document to approve.

If extending the taproom app is the wrong call, say so now. Otherwise I'll write it up.
